items.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018
items.q: And I remember Bob Mann, who’s dad used to be the piano player or something on the Arthur Godfrey Show, Bob Mann played with everybody. Well Taylor, James Taylor. He was with him for years. Perfect pitch. And he asked me one day... he said, “Who did that arrangement of ‘Lonesome Suzie?’” I said, “I

ctx.x: I’m telling you, some of that music, those horn parts and stuff just made a profound effect on me. And sometimes it was those dissonances that resolve, and I would go to the piano and go what is that. And so I just wanted to, as I said early on I’ve been waiting to talk to you since 1969 so I could say that.

No but as you just started to talk I almost start to feel like crying because it reminded me, maybe, of when I was in the studio and we finally heard it back, I’ve felt this with a couple of my arrangements. This is just me. I’m a sensitive person. Sometimes I don’t like being so sensitive. I’m not always. But I almost cried listening to my arrangement because it’s very powerful. It starts out with a whisper, there is nothing, just him and a bass. And it builds. And the middle part where it starts to make the…
Well thanks for sharing that with me. You’ve made an impression on a lot of people.
